claims.statement: For an acetate-producing pulse window, if the lower confidence bound on methyl-13C acetate molecules exceeds the upper bound on all distinct old-13C atoms that could have occupied a reactive CO precursor state during that window (plus background/contamination), then a topology in which both carbons at every C-C-forming event enter as CO is impossible.
assumptions: The labeled-acetate lower bound and all atom-budget upper bounds use the same molar basis and collection interval.
The CO-accessible upper bound includes all adsorption geometries, DIC and cell hold-up, feed leakage, unresolved carbon pools, and any preloaded CH2 label that can re-enter reactive CO.
No carbon-13 enters from an unmeasured source beyond the listed feed, impurity, and background terms.
claims.novelty_boundary: A mathematical decision certificate, not an observed route, new molecule, or external discovery. The key assay premise has not been demonstrated on Cu18 or Cu-Fe.
claims.costs: Requires isotope feed and valve calibration, full DIC/gas/surface/product mass balance, isotope-edited operando Raman across four CO site classes, time-fractionated positional acetate assay, high-bandwidth electrochemistry, and response-kernel/power analysis. Money, hours, energy, and quantities are UNKNOWN pending SI, instrument limits, and pilot data.
claims.falsifier: A validated experiment returns methyl-13C acetate lower bound no greater than the complete all-CO label budget, or shows no interval with persistent labeled CH2 and a sufficiently small CO-accessible label budget.
claims.next_gate: No-product Cu18 pilot must calibrate label transfer and show a nonempty selective window; otherwise retain UNKNOWN and stop the confirmatory assay.

claims.statement: The 2025 Cu18 operando/Raman paper does not provide measured 13C precursor pools, isotope-edited assignments, positional acetate time traces, or a bound on old-label transfer back into reactive CO; therefore its published observations do not establish the intervention gate or identify the direct CH2-CO topology against a CO-CO competitor.
assumptions: Scope is the published main article and its stated data availability, checked 2026-10-08.
claims.status: source audit; absence from inspected article text and data statement
claims.novelty_boundary: Negative scope statement about inspected publication; raw supporting information was not obtained in this cycle, so specific methods details may reside there.
claims.costs: Acquire and review supporting information and request raw time-resolved spectra/current from the corresponding author; this is data acquisition and may have nonzero staff/access cost.
claims.falsifier: Retrieved supporting information or author-provided dataset contains the missing isotope-calibrated precursor measurements and complete transient bounds.
claims.next_gate: Obtain SI and raw data before final wet-lab design; repeat source audit if these data become available.

claims.statement: At 298.15 K, equal-prefactor TST applied to the source-reported Cu(100) activation-energy gaps 1.22-(0.81 or 0.76) eV predicts symmetric CO-CO/direct CH2-CO rate ratios 1.17e-7 or 1.68e-8, respectively.
assumptions: Use the source's static Cu(100) barriers without surface/potential correction.
Assume equal prefactors and equal relevant reactant coverages.
claims.status: internally calculated conditional implication from source-reported DFT parameters
claims.novelty_boundary: Does not validate DFT, provide an operando route fraction, or transfer to Cu-Fe/CuBi/other Cu surfaces.
claims.costs: Elementary exponent evaluation; no experimental or compute costs beyond exact numeric arithmetic.
claims.falsifier: Not applicable to the conditional arithmetic; the equal-prefactor/coverage premises can fail physically.
claims.next_gate: Treat only as source-model context; do not use as an empirical rate prediction.

claims.statement: Using the source's eight-electron acetate stoichiometry and Faraday's constant, the 10, 20, and 200 mA cm-2 current densities imply charge-only upper bounds of 12.96, 25.91, and 259.11 nmol acetate s-1 cm-2 if all charge formed acetate.
assumptions: All current is Faradaic and assigned to acetate, giving an upper bound only.
One acetate molecule requires eight electrons.
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact stoichiometric upper bound
claims.novelty_boundary: No absolute acetate FE or actual product rate is inferred.
claims.costs: Formula evaluation only; real product limit requires measured acetate FE and collection/NMR sensitivity.
claims.falsifier: Not applicable to the upper-bound arithmetic; measured FE can only reduce the actual rate.
claims.next_gate: Measure acetate FE and assay recovery in a pilot to set area-time and replication.

overall_status: conditional intervention certificate defined; physical separability UNKNOWN; no new breakthrough claimed
